title_en: The Photo Booth Took My Hand
story_zh: 閃光後，我的拇指不見了。那晚，我在日本一座小車站等末班車。候車室角落，有台亮著燈的老拍貼機。離發車還有十分鐘，我投幣坐了進去。第一張照片裡，我舉起的右手少了拇指。我低頭一看，掌邊也只剩平滑的皮膚。不流血，也不痛，像從來沒有長過。螢幕跳出兩個字：重拍。我想把手拍回來，便按了那個按鈕。第二次閃光後，整隻右手都消失了。袖口下面，手腕變成封死的圓頭。我終於明白，重拍只會刪掉更多身體。我掀開布簾，卻被安全帶猛地拉回。剛坐下時，椅子上根本沒有安全帶。螢幕自己開始倒數：三，二。我用左手扯斷插頭，閃光燈熄了。安全帶鬆開，我衝到月台找站員。他看見我的手腕，立刻拉下候車室鐵門。鐵門裡，機器仍用我的聲音說著：重拍。我搭上末班車，右手卻永遠沒有回來。
story_en: The flash stole my thumb. I was waiting for the last train in Japan. An old photo booth stood in the waiting room. With ten minutes left, I paid and sat down. In the first photo, my raised hand had no thumb. I looked down. Smooth skin covered its place. No blood. No pain. As though it never existed. The screen offered another picture. I pressed the button, hoping to get it back. The second flash took my entire right hand. My wrist ended in a smooth stump. Another picture would only erase more of me. I lifted the curtain. The seat belt pulled me back. There had been no belt when I sat down. The screen began counting down. Three. Two. I pulled the plug. The flash died. The belt loosened. I ran to the station attendant. He saw my wrist and locked the waiting room. Inside, it said, "Another picture," in my voice. I caught the last train. My hand never returned.
